artworks.title: Aeneas, Anchises, and Ascanius
artworks.description: Bernini's Borghese marble: Aeneas carries Anchises from burning Troy while Ascanius follows — three generations in one spiral of flight.

artworks.title: Aeneas' Flight from Troy
artworks.description: Barocci's Borghese canvas: Aeneas bears Anchises through the sack, Ascanius beside him, Creusa behind — Virgil's departure from the flames.

artworks.title: Aeneas Fleeing from Troy
artworks.description: Batoni's neoclassical flight: the Trojan house leaves Ilion with the Penates — exile as polished Roman destiny.

artworks.title: Aeneas Rescuing Anchises from Burning Troy
artworks.description: Elsheimer's night fire: Aeneas carries Anchises out of Troy's blaze — the sack reduced to a small copper of flame and piety.

music.title: Les Troyens
music.description: Berlioz's Virgilian opera opens with Troy's fall and Aeneas' flight — the survivor who must leave the burning city for Italy.

popCulture.title: Aeneas
popCulture.description: Troy's survivor who carries Anchises and the gods — Aeneas' flight remains Rome's founding exile.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Books II–III turn the sack into departure — the city burns while destiny points west.
